claim: There is no easy button for life: so much of it boils down to our willingness and ability to do hard shit, the only way to grow and progress meaningfully
"Hard is just another word for new"
All growth lies on the other side of hard things, some more challenging than others
One of the best things we can do is intentionally practice hard things, not just where we kind of have to
A business, job or managing-people challenge probably takes hard stuff to grow through, and one of the best ways through is hard situations in physical training
Physical training transfers to the rest of your life: train to discomfort, readjust and keep going until it sinks in that you can exist there; practiced regularly, it translates

Physical training to discomfort is facing resistance "in an arena of your choosing at a time of your choosing", to show him who's the boss, so tomorrow, at your job or business, resistance is still there, but you're a little more powerful against him, and he comes in feeling a little worse about himself because you kicked his ass in the physical arena
For men, physical training is about so much more than looks: mind, emotions, success, drive, hormones, relationships, everything is affected, negatively by inactivity or extremely positively
name: Why men train

claim: Physical training helps the best man we all want to be bring what lives inside into the physical world, body change or not
name: Why men train

claim: In physical training, the harder the thing, the more you can benefit and the stronger you can be when you face it
Fun in your workout may mean you're not on the right path, until, the awesome thing, you have fun being uncomfortable, once you really do that a lot and get into that mindset
Some climbing workouts were just climbing to tunes. That, or a run where you feel awesome, differs a lot from pushing until really uncomfortable, then deciding to keep going
Listen to your body and know pushing really hard from injury: you can push way harder than you think without injury, or too far, into injury

The suggestion is not to ignore your body's signs but to get uncomfortable, decide it's okay and keep going, in push-ups, pull-ups, climbing, running, lifting, whatever, chosen as your intention beforehand
You can't necessarily go this hard, pushing into discomfort, every day forever: you need active recovery days, and our bodies kind of go in cycles a little bit
As often as you can, go in with the one goal to "push until I get as uncomfortable as I can get"
Try to break yourself: if an extreme enough physical effort has never kind of broken you down mentally and emotionally, you haven't pushed yourself
Push hard enough in physical effort and emotional stuff will all of a sudden come up, a part of you that you're not facing
Strong advice: decide before some workouts that your only goal is to push until discomfort
In a workout, discomfort is when the workout starts, everything before is warming up, and every minute there pays huge dividends, in body and life
A promise: spend time in discomfort and you'll feel the benefits, if you're willing to put in the work
Life comes down to: are you willing?
Plenty of life was spent unwilling, and the question "are you willing?" applies to sharing this message too
Are you willing to put in the work, physical too, for the change and growth you want? We either are or aren't
If we're willing, the most power can be found through choosing intentional discomfort: decide it's okay, your friend, your power, because it is
All our power lies in the hard shit in our life
It's cliche, but a lot of cliches are true: all our strength lies in our hardest times

One of the greatest periods of growth came when his son, about a week and a half old, had open heart surgery, then three months in the ICU and a year or so of recovery. Watching him fight and almost lose, as a kid really, was by a wide margin the hardest experience to that point, still top two or three, and the time of the very most growth

Life as software versions: like iOS or Android, the dot versions, one point two, one point six, 13.2, 13.4, are usually minor security fixes; the big changes come with the next whole version, six to seven. Habits and intention make incremental gains, but a major update to the you that you are only comes through difficulty, "the reality of life"
Recognizing that difficulty is our friend, you can make the major updates of you happen and push the minor updates along faster
Do hard stuff, your own way
Just for today, forget the future: you can only live today
Find discomfort in the physical arena today, maybe bodyweight squats, a plank as long as you can and then a whole lot longer, push-ups, climbing or running: it will pay off
